sections.paragraph: Acute COVID-19 is the illness caused by a current SARS-CoV-2 infection. Its course ranges from mild respiratory symptoms to severe illness, with older age and certain medical conditions increasing risk. Drug studies have tested ways to reduce viral replication or the harmful host response before illness progresses. The treatment question depends on the phase and severity of illness. Early outpatient antiviral treatment targets viral replication within a short period after symptom onset, whereas a hospitalized-patient study addresses a different clinical setting. COVID-OUT examined metformin, ivermectin and fluvoxamine in nonhospitalized adults with overweight or obesity. RECOVERY tested hydroxychloroquine in hospitalized patients. Neither the population nor the endpoint can be assumed to transfer between those settings. Research on progression during the infection is also distinct from later follow-up for Long COVID: preventing an acute event, shortening symptoms and reducing a future diagnosis are separate clinical goals.

None significantly reduced its primary composite of hypoxemia, emergency care, hospitalization or death. Nirmatrelvir with ritonavir has a separate established role in early treatment of eligible people at higher risk of severe COVID-19. Other cited studies address different repurposing questions. PRINCIPLE found no clinically meaningful recovery or hospitalization benefit from doxycycline in older or vulnerable community patients. The higher-dose ACTIV-6 fluvoxamine trial did not accelerate sustained symptom recovery. RECOVERY found no reduction in 28-day mortality from hydroxychloroquine in hospitalized patients. Early antiviral treatment also has a short window from symptom onset. An early-treatment recommendation therefore includes both eligibility and the ability to use the medicine safely with a person's existing regimen. The ritonavir component is especially relevant when reviewing other prescriptions, rather than treating a positive SARS-CoV-2 test as sufficient reason to use the combination. Kidney and liver function are separate considerations that affect treatment selection within the short treatment window. The cited outpatient guidance addresses eligible people at higher risk of progression, so the suitability assessment belongs to that population and timing. The COVID-OUT trial and outpatient antiviral recommendations concern different drugs, eligibility criteria and outcomes. Its composite also combines oxygen measurements with health-care use and death, so a composite result is not a precise mortality estimate. sections.paragraph: Glioblastoma is an aggressive glioma that infiltrates brain tissue, making complete removal difficult even when surgery is feasible. Care commonly combines surgery with radiation and chemotherapy; research on repurposed medicines asks whether another drug can improve that treatment rather than replace it. Mebendazole was tested with temozolomide in a phase 1 study of 24 people with high-grade gliomas, including 18 with glioblastoma. Its purpose was dose, exposure and tolerability assessment, without a randomized temozolomide-only comparator. Other clinical records concern recurrent disease or different combinations: disulfiram did not significantly improve survival and increased severe adverse events, while an uncontrolled atorvastatin study did not demonstrate improved six-month progression-free survival. These findings need their separate tumor populations, background treatments and endpoints, rather than one general claim that repurposing improves glioblastoma outcomes.

sections.paragraph: Mebendazole has been investigated as an addition to chemotherapy, with different studies addressing feasibility and survival. The initial phase 1 study examined drug exposure and tolerability in 24 people with high-grade gliomas; it did not establish an added survival effect against temozolomide alone. A later trial reported nine-month survival of 36.6% with temozolomide plus mebendazole and 45% with lomustine plus mebendazole. Both groups received mebendazole, and neither reached the prespecified 55% benchmark, so the comparison does not isolate its contribution. The other cited clinical approaches were also unsuccessful in demonstrating their intended improvement: disulfiram did not significantly improve survival, and a single-arm atorvastatin study did not demonstrate better six-month progression-free survival. These are distinct clinical questions, not interchangeable evidence of one anticancer effect.

sections.paragraph: ME/CFS is a disabling multisystem illness marked by reduced ability to carry out usual activities, unrefreshing sleep and post-exertional malaise. Physical or mental effort can cause a delayed worsening of symptoms. Naltrexone research has examined altered signaling in natural-killer immune cells as one possible treatment target. The selected treatment research should be distinguished from the illness definition. A natural-killer-cell study examined TRPM3 channel currents in nine people already taking naltrexone and nine healthy controls. It did not randomize ME/CFS patients to treatment or measure recovery. Three separate patient-compiled case histories described variable symptoms during naltrexone use, including one account of improved pain and sleep without improved function. Those observations do not establish that one immune pathway explains the whole illness. The condition's reduced activity and delayed post-exertional worsening remain clinical concerns that a cell measurement alone cannot resolve.

The TRPM3 study examined natural-killer cells from nine people already taking naltrexone and nine healthy controls; channel currents resembled those in control cells. It did not randomize treated and untreated patients or measure recovery, daily function or post-exertional malaise. Three separate patient-compiled case histories described variable symptom changes. One reported better pain and sleep without better function, making those outcomes important to distinguish. sections.paragraph: PGAD/genitopelvic dysesthesia involves unwanted genital arousal sensations that persist or recur without corresponding sexual desire. Symptoms can be distressing and are not evidence of unusually high libido. Neurological studies investigate sensory signaling from the genital area, pelvis and sacral nerves, rather than assuming a single psychological or behavioral cause. The distinction shapes both evaluation and treatment research. A person can experience unwanted genital sensations without wanting sexual activity; measuring sexual desire or repetitive behavior alone would miss that defining feature. The neurological case series included medication-associated symptoms and underlying nerve or spinal pathology, while the iPGAD case-control study examined clinical characteristics. These designs help investigate possible contributors rather than establish a single cause for every person. They also do not demonstrate that naltrexone relieves the sensations. Trials of that medicine in compulsive sexual behavior address impaired control of behavior, which is a different condition and cannot be used as a substitute PGAD treatment result.

sections.paragraph: Periodontitis involves inflammation and destruction of the tissues and bone that support teeth. Bacterial plaque initiates the problem, while the body's inflammatory response contributes to tissue damage; removing plaque and influencing the host response therefore address related but different parts of the disease. Subantimicrobial-dose doxycycline has been investigated to inhibit tissue-degrading host enzymes alongside scaling and root planing. A multicenter study found additional improvement in clinical attachment and periodontal pocket depth when the medicine was added to the same mechanical treatment given to the control group. Rapamycin research addresses another host-response hypothesis, but its periodontal bone findings came from aged female mice. An animal bone response cannot establish a human periodontal regimen or substitute for the clinical evidence and local care relevant to people with periodontitis.

sections.paragraph: Alzheimer’s disease disrupts communication between neurons, damages their connections and ultimately causes cell death. Inflammation involving brain immune cells is one process investigated as a treatment target. This disease process extends beyond normal age-related changes in thinking because neuronal connections and brain function become widely damaged. A separate small thalidomide trial in mild-to-moderate disease also found no cognitive benefit and had poor tolerability. These are patient-outcome questions rather than evidence that reducing an inflammatory signal necessarily changes the course of illness. The population, duration and ability to continue treatment all matter when interpreting whether an experimental approach affects meaningful disease outcomes.

sections.paragraph: Sarcopenia involves declining muscle strength and function, often with reduced muscle mass. Difficulty rising from a chair, slower walking and increased falls can threaten independence. Resistance activity and adequate nutrition are central to preserving muscle health. This makes the endpoint important when evaluating a repurposed medicine: walking performance, strength and muscle size are related but different measures. These studies challenge a general assumption that improving metabolism necessarily improves muscle aging. Their selected populations and interventions should remain distinct, with physical function assessed directly rather than inferred solely from a change in muscle mass.
